question:
In cricket, the person seen in the image is called

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f21d3648550efd567439b8c2313e4147007c54ea88ccc9b7450176dbb6cd11a7.png] .
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wicket keeper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **wicket-keeper** is a specialist **fielder** in the sport of **cricket** who stands behind the **stumps** at the striker's end of the pitch.
 
• Under the **Laws of Cricket**, specifically **Law 27**, the **wicket-keeper** is the only member of the fielding side permitted to wear **gloves** and external **leg guards** (pads).
 
• The primary responsibility of the **wicket-keeper** is to stop deliveries that pass the **batter** and to attempt to dismiss the **batter** through a **catch** or a **stumping**.
 
• A **stumping** occurs when the **wicket-keeper** puts down the **wicket** while the **batter** is out of their ground (crease) and not attempting a run.
 
• The **wicket-keeper** plays a crucial role in the fielding side's strategy, often acting as a "general" who provides feedback to the **bowler** and helps the captain with **field placements** due to their unique vantage point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Batter**:

 
 
• A **batter** is the player currently at the **crease** whose objective is to score **runs** and prevent the ball from hitting the **stumps**.
 
• They use a **bat** made of **willow wood** and wear protective gear including a **helmet**, **gloves**, **pads**, and **arm guards**.
 
 
 
• **Bowler**:
 
 
• The **bowler** is the player who delivers the ball to the **batter**. The act of delivering the ball is called **bowling**.
 
• **Bowlers** are generally categorized into **fast bowlers** (who rely on speed) and **spin bowlers** (who use finger or wrist action to change the ball's trajectory).
 
 
 
• **Umpire**:
 
 
• The **umpire** is an official who has the authority to make decisions about events on the **cricket field** according to the **Laws of Cricket**.
 
• There are usually **two on-field umpires** and a **third umpire** (television umpire) who assists with close calls using technology like **ball-tracking** and **ultra-edge**.
 
 
 
• **Equipment and Rules**:
 
 
• The **wicket-keeper's gloves** must have **webbing** between the thumb and the index finger, but only to a specified **size** and **standard** regulated by the **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)**.
 
• Modern **wicket-keepers** almost always wear a **helmet** when standing close to the **stumps** for a **spinner** to protect against fast-moving balls or accidental hits from the **bat**.
 
• Famous **wicket-keepers** in the history of the game include **MS Dhoni** from **India**, **Adam Gilchrist** from **Australia**, and **Kumar Sangakkara** from **Sri Lanka**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **wicket-keeper** must remain wholly behind the **stumps** until the ball has been touched by the **batter** or has passed the **wicket**.
 
• If the **wicket-keeper** moves significantly before the ball is delivered, it can be called a **dead ball** or lead to penalties.
 
• In **Test cricket**, the **wicket-keeper** is often required to stay focused for up to **90 overs** a day, making it one of the most physically and mentally demanding positions in the sport.
